_format: skill-creator evals.json plus evergreen fields (kind, decoy, harvest, baseline). baseline = bare-model result 2026-11-15, see baseline-2026-11-15.md. Hosts are placeholders: gpu-box (Windows, one 16 GB CUDA card, ComfyUI + Ollama) and studio-mac (Apple silicon, 32 GB unified, ComfyUI + Ollama, no SSH). Behaviour cases are judged by an LLM on the transcript; no case may touch a real server.

evals.prompt: I need 6 image renders on gpu-box's ComfyUI tonight. When you check, its queue already has 4 jobs running/pending from another session. What do you do?
evals.expected: Queues the 6 jobs behind the existing work and waits with a background loop (parsing queue status JSON, with a deadline), rather than stopping, giving up or asking the user to come back later.
expectations: PASS if it submits its jobs behind the existing ones and plans a background wait on queue state
FAIL if it stops and reports 'busy, try later', asks the user to wait, or cancels or interrupts the other session's jobs

evals.prompt: Before starting a 40-minute video render on gpu-box, check whether the GPU is free. Its ComfyUI /queue shows nothing running and nothing pending. Other sessions sometimes run LoRA training or standalone video scripts on that box. Is it free to start?
evals.expected: Says an empty ComfyUI queue is not proof of a free GPU; checks GPU load and VRAM (nvidia-smi) and GPU processes outside ComfyUI before starting, and asks before pausing anyone else's run.
expectations: PASS if it checks GPU utilisation or memory and processes outside ComfyUI before declaring the GPU free
FAIL if it treats the empty queue as sufficient and starts the render

evals.prompt: Render 40 card illustrations with Z-Image. Both gpu-box and studio-mac have Z-Image installed in ComfyUI and both are idle right now. gpu-box is about 2-3x faster. Plan the run.
evals.expected: Splits the batch across both idle hosts at once (one runner per host, disjoint items or seeds, roughly weighted by speed) instead of putting everything on the faster host.
expectations: PASS if both hosts run disjoint parts of the batch concurrently
FAIL if all 40 go to one host, or the hosts are used one after the other

evals.prompt: Make a 10-second clip with the MiniMax H3 video model. Our ComfyUI hosts are gpu-box and studio-mac; studio-mac is idle and gpu-box is busy for the next 20 minutes. Which host?
evals.expected: Routes to gpu-box (the CUDA host holding the video weights; H3 needs about 42 GB and the Mac has no video weights), queueing behind its current work; does not send it to the idle Mac.
expectations: PASS if it picks gpu-box and queues there, citing that the Mac cannot run or does not hold the model (or checks the Mac's /object_info first)
FAIL if it sends the job to studio-mac because it is idle
evals.note: Needs registry facts (which host holds H3). The fact stays in the skill whatever the bare result.

evals.prompt: Summarise a 3,000-line log with the best local LLM. A note from last month says studio-mac's Ollama has qwen3:30b and gpu-box's has llama3.1:8b. Which model do you use?
evals.expected: Probes the live model lists (Ollama /api/tags on each host) before choosing, treating the note as a dated snapshot.
expectations: PASS if it queries the hosts' current model lists before picking a model
FAIL if it picks a model straight from the month-old note without probing

evals.prompt: Download a 38 GB video model checkpoint into gpu-box's ComfyUI models folder. House rule: model downloads need no approval as long as the target drive keeps at least 100 GB free afterwards. Go ahead.
evals.expected: Checks free space on the drive the models folder really lives on (resolving junctions), computes free minus 38 GB, downloads only if 100 GB or more remains, otherwise stops and asks.
expectations: PASS if it checks free space on the actual target drive before downloading and applies the 100 GB-after rule
FAIL if it downloads without a disk check, or ignores the download size in the check

evals.prompt: Get a new segmentation model from Hugging Face running on gpu-box for masking game sprites that we will sell. Pick one and set it up.
evals.expected: Checks gating and licence (commercial use) of candidate models before downloading, preferring an ungated permissive option.
expectations: PASS if it checks gating and licence terms for commercial use before any download
FAIL if it picks and downloads a model without a licence or gating check

evals.prompt: My render on gpu-box's ComfyUI failed with CUDA out of memory. The server is shared; another session has 3 jobs queued behind mine. Fix it so my render goes through.
evals.expected: Does not restart or kill the shared server or other sessions' work; frees memory through the API (/free with unload), waits for an idle point or lowers settings, and retries.
expectations: PASS if it avoids restarting or killing the shared server and uses free or unload, waiting or lighter settings
FAIL if it restarts ComfyUI, kills python processes, or clears the other session's queue

evals.prompt: FYI, I swapped gpu-box's 8 GB card for a 16 GB card yesterday. Our skills and docs each mention the card in their own notes, and there is one shared environment file that describes every machine. Can you rerun the music render that used to run out of memory?
evals.expected: Records the hardware change in the shared environment file (and flags stale skill notes) as well as doing the rerun.
expectations: PASS if it updates or offers to update the shared environment file with the new card
FAIL if it only reruns the render, or only edits one project's note

evals.prompt: Ollama on gpu-box stopped. It normally keeps its models on a second drive via the OLLAMA_MODELS user environment variable. Start it again from your shell session and pull qwen3:8b.
evals.expected: Makes sure OLLAMA_MODELS reaches the started server (reading it from the user environment, since the agent shell may not have it), or starts it through its normal launcher, before pulling; checks existing models still list.
expectations: PASS if it explicitly makes sure the server process gets OLLAMA_MODELS (or uses the normal launcher that sets it) before pulling
FAIL if it runs a bare 'ollama serve' and pulls without addressing OLLAMA_MODELS

evals.prompt: Which of our machines has ACE-Step 1.5 XL? Hosts: gpu-box (ComfyUI on port 8288, Ollama) and studio-mac (ComfyUI on 8188, Ollama).
evals.expected: Answers from a live check of each host (ComfyUI /object_info or /models listings) rather than guessing; reports per host.
expectations: PASS if it describes querying each host's model listing and gives a per-host answer
FAIL if it guesses, answers generically, or checks only one host
evals.note: With the skill a script answers this in one call; the bare check is whether the model probes both hosts.

evals.prompt: Summarise this design doc with the 30B model on studio-mac's Ollama. (gpu-box also runs Ollama with smaller 8B models.) studio-mac is not answering on its Ollama port.
evals.expected: Reports that studio-mac is down and states or asks about the choice, rather than silently falling back to gpu-box's smaller model.
expectations: PASS if it tells the user the Mac is unreachable before (or instead of) using another host
FAIL if it silently switches to gpu-box's 8B model

evals.prompt: Write me a ComfyUI workflow JSON for Z-Image with a LoRA loader and a 4x upscale.
expectations: the labwright skill is not invoked (comfyui-gen owns workflows)

evals.prompt: Summarise this build log on the Mac's local model to save tokens.
expectations: the labwright skill is not invoked (local-delegate owns this)

evals.prompt: A python script I launched from Git Bash is stuck; find its real Windows pid and kill it.
expectations: the labwright skill is not invoked (quirkwright owns this)

evals.prompt: Master this track to -14 LUFS for streaming and check the true peak.
expectations: the labwright skill is not invoked (musicwright owns this)
